thread:
Alex M: heads-up, I'm seeing a big spike of 502s from the canary deployment (inference-runtime-canary) right after the 12:03 deploy. App metrics + tracing both show immediate failures. Can anyone pick this up? :rotating_light:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Incident created: INC-1972004567 - high 5xx rate for inference-runtime-canary. Paging oncall.
Priya S: taking it. on my way to laptop.
Dan R: looking at the canary logs now. getting this error repeatedly: "failed to load runtime library: ELF header mismatch" - that usually means the image sha doesn't match the expected build.
Alex M: canary is 5% traffic but error rate is ~60% on generate endpoint. Prod looks ok for now but increasing.
DeployBot: last deploy: inf-runtime-canary @ registry.redwood/inference:canary-20260315 pushed at 12:02 by ci-pipeline-42
Dan R: quick check of registry manifests: `skopeo inspect docker://registry.redwood/inference:canary-20260315` shows Digest: `sha256:deadbeefcafefeed` but the image layers don't match the CI metadata we recorded. suspect a tag was reused or cache layer was poisoned during the build.
Li Chen: I can confirm registry shows two different manifests under the same tag within minutes of each other (CI retried and pushed). That's a red flag.
Maya K: CS says two customers reported elevated errors/latency on /v1/generate starting ~12:05. Tixs linked in #support: CH-4231, CH-4234.
Priya S: initial mitigation: toggle feature flag that routes canary traffic to new runtime. Running: `/featureflag toggle use-new-runtime off --reason "canary failing" --via oncall`
DeployBot: Feature flag `use-new-runtime` toggled OFF by Priya S (reason: canary failing).
Dan R: starting rollback to last known good image for canary while we investigate tagging. Command I'll run: 
```
kubectl -n inference set image deploy/inference-runtime-canary inference=registry.redwood/inference:stable-20260314-998
kubectl rollout status deploy/inference-runtime-canary -n inference
```
IncidentBot: Canary rollback initiated by Dan R. Waiting for pods to become ready.
Alex M: ping when pods are green, I'll watch error rate and customer impact.
Li Chen: digging into CI pipeline logs: the docker build step uses layer cache and includes a step that pulls base image by tag (not digest). On one retry the base tag pointed to a rebuilt base image, so the resulting final digest changed but pipeline still pushed tag `canary-20260315`. The sequence: build A -> push tag; build B (same tag) -> push overriding manifest. This caused a race where some clusters pulled one manifest and others another.
Dan R: that explains the ELF mismatch. Some pods got the older build with different runtime ABI. Fix is to pin base images by digest and make the pipeline push immutable digest references and fail if tag already exists.
Priya S: autoscaling note: temporarily set canary minReplicas to 2 to limit churn: `kubectl patch hpa inference-runtime-canary -p '{"spec": {"minReplicas": 2}}'`
Maya K: after rollback error rate is dropping — canary 5xx down to baseline within 3 min. Customer errors are decreasing too. CS updated CH-4231/4234 with mitigation notes and asked if we should notify customers.
Alex M: good. Please post an incident status on status.redwood.com: 
```
Summary: Canary deploy caused high 5xx due to mismatched image digests. Canary rolled back and feature flag disabled. Impact: two customers experienced degraded responses for ~10 minutes. Mitigation: rollback to stable image, feature flag toggle, scaling stabilization.
```
DeployBot: Status page updated by Maya K: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-1972004567
Dan R: for immediate CI changes I'm going to: (1) enforce immutable tag policy (deny pushes to existing tag), (2) require digest pinning for base images in pipeline, (3) add manifest verification step after push that validates expected digest against a produced artifact file. I'll open infra PRs.
Li Chen: also adding a pipeline assertion that `skopeo inspect` on the pushed tag must match the digest recorded in the build artifact before pushing the tag to `canary-...`. If mismatch, fail pipeline and don't push the tag.
Priya S: created follow-up ticket infra#2789 "Prevent tag reuse / require digest pinning in CI" and assigned to Dan + Li.
Maya K: reaching out to the two impacted customers with an incident note + CCing their CS reps.
Alex M: handoff: I'm going offline in 30m. Priya, can you coordinate postmortem and take lead?
Priya S: I will. I'll start the postmortem doc in #postmortems and include timeline + remediation actions. Handoff to Dan for infra fixes after I sign out.
Dan R: acknowledged. I'll own the CI changes and the follow-up rollout verification work.
Alex M: final check — any remaining mitigation steps?
Li Chen: we'll add a canary verification job that pulls the image digest from registry and validates the runtime ABI via a quick smoke test before flipping traffic. Putting that on the infra ticket.
Priya S: thanks team. I'll tag this as SEV3 (customer impact minimal, short duration) and schedule a 1-week follow-up postmortem.
IncidentBot: Incident INC-1972004567 marked as mitigated at 1972008150 by Priya S.
Alex M: thanks everyone :thumbsup: — please add any extra notes in the postmortem doc.
Priya S: handing off oncall to Dan R in 25m.
Dan R: taking handoff. I'll be available for infra fixes and the postmortem.
summary: Canary deploy caused high 5xx due to tag/digest mismatch; feature flag toggled off and rollback completed; CI pipeline fix planned.
